title: How the Ozone Layer Shields Life From UV
description: What the ozone layer does, how CFCs damaged it and what the Antarctic ozone hole is, from NASA and NOAA.
narration: What shields life on Earth from the Sun's most harmful ultraviolet rays? A thin layer of ozone acts as a sunscreen for the whole planet. Its job is absorbing UV-B, the most harmful ultraviolet radiation reaching the surface. It sits in the stratosphere, roughly 11 to 50 kilometres above the surface. In the 1970s, scientists found that man-made CFC chemicals were destroying it. A single chlorine atom can destroy ozone repeatedly, as many as 100,000 times. The so-called hole is really a thin patch of depleted ozone over Antarctica. Because CFCs linger in the air, they will keep affecting the ozone layer well into this century.
